questions.question: Who called the preamble of the Indian Constitution ‘The Political Horoscope of our Constitution’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. KM Munshi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. KM Munshi** referred to the preamble of the Indian Constitution as 'The Political Horoscope of our Constitution'.
 
• The preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and outlines the guiding principles and philosophy of the document.
 
• It reflects the aspirations and values of the people of India, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• The preamble plays a crucial role in interpreting the Constitution and understanding the intent of its framers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The preamble is considered an integral part of the Constitution and has been referred to in various landmark judgments by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Dr. KM Munshi was a prominent member of the Constituent Assembly and played a significant role in drafting the Constitution.
 
• The preamble has been amended once by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, which added the words 'socialist', 'secular', and 'integrity'.

questions.question: At which place is Harappan Dockyard found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lothal**__

__

• Lothal is located in the present-day state of **Gujarat, India**.
 
• The dockyard at Lothal is considered one of the world's earliest known docks and was crucial for maritime trade in ancient times.
 
• This dockyard connected the city to an ancient course of the Sabarmati river, which was crucial for trade and commerce.
 
• The discovery of the dockyard has provided significant insights into the engineering and maritime skills of the Harappan people.

• It flourished in the basins of the Indus River, which flows through present-day Pakistan, and along the Ghaggar-Hakra River, which once flowed through northwest India and eastern Pakistan.
 
• Other major Harappan sites include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Rakhigarhi**.
 
• The civilization is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Artifacts such as seals, pottery, and jewelry found at Harappan sites provide valuable insights into the culture and daily life of the people.

questions.question: Which chromosome is involved in the production of ‘masked’ mRNAs for early development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lampbrush chromosome**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lampbrush chromosomes** are involved in the production of 'masked' mRNAs for early development.
 
• These chromosomes are a special form of chromosome found in the growing oocytes (immature egg cells) of most animals, except mammals.
 
• The lampbrush chromosomes are characterized by their large size and distinctive appearance, which is due to the extensive looping of chromatin.
 
• They play a crucial role in gene transcription during early development, producing mRNAs that are stored and later used during embryogenesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Masked mRNAs** are mRNA molecules that are transcribed but not immediately translated into proteins; they are stored in the cytoplasm and translated at a later stage.
 
• The structure of lampbrush chromosomes allows for high levels of transcriptional activity, which is necessary for the rapid cell divisions and developmental processes in early embryogenesis.
 
• Lampbrush chromosomes were first observed by Walther Flemming in 1882, and their detailed structure was later described by Ruckert in 1892.
 
• The study of lampbrush chromosomes has provided significant insights into the organization and function of chromatin and the regulation of gene expression.

• **Ram Navami** is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Chaitra**.
 
• It marks the birth of **Lord Rama**, the seventh avatar of the deity Vishnu.
 
• The festival typically falls in the Gregorian months of **March or April**.
 
• Devotees celebrate the day with fasting, reading the **Ramayana**, and participating in **processions and prayers**.
 
• The day is considered highly auspicious and is observed with great devotion across India.

• The epic **Ramayana**, which narrates the life of Lord Rama, is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient Indian literature, the other being the **Mahabharata**.
 
• The celebrations of Ram Navami also include **recitals of devotional hymns and kirtans** in praise of Lord Rama.
 
• In some regions, **Ratha Yatra** (chariot procession) is organized, where the idols of Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman are taken out in a grand procession.

**The value of x is ₹3,000.**

Marked price (MP) is 20% higher than the cost price (CP).

Discount allowed is 10%.

Profit Percentage = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/(Cost Price) times 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = CP + 20% of CP

⇒ MP = 100 + (20/100) × 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 20

⇒ MP = 120

Selling Price (SP) = MP - 10% of MP

⇒ SP = 120 - (10/100) × 120

⇒ SP = 120 - 12

⇒ SP = 108

Profit = SP - CP

⇒ Profit = 108 - 100

⇒ Profit = 8

Profit Percentage = (Profit)/(Cost Price) times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (8)/(100) times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 8%

Eat like a bird

options.text: Nobody can eat with Jerry at the same table as he is so messy
The colonial powers colonised small countries by exploiting them and stealing their resources.
Pinky is on a diet so she is too picky about the food she eats.
Overeating is the most obvious reason for gaining weight quickly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **'****Pinky is on a diet so she is too picky about the food she eats.****'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"eat like a bird"** means to eat very little or be very picky about food. (बहुत कम खाना)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite the lavish spread, she **ate like a bird** at the party.
 
 
 
• 
 **Sentence 3** implies that **Pinky is eating very little** because she is on a diet and is picky about the food she consumes, which aligns with the meaning of the idiom.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Nobody can eat with Jerry at the same table as he is so messy.**

 
 
• **Explanation: **This sentence describes a messy eater but does not use the idiom "eat like a bird" correctly.
 
 
 
• **The colonial powers colonized small countries by exploiting them and stealing their resources.**
 
 
• **Explanation: **This sentence talks about colonization and exploitation, which is unrelated to the idiom "eat like a bird".
 
 
 
• **Overeating is the most obvious reason for gaining weight quickly.**
 
 
• **Explanation: **This sentence discusses overeating, which is the opposite of "eating like a bird".

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

'I have been to Australia,' Amritha told me.

options.text: Amritha told me that she had been to Australia.
Amritha told me that she has be to Australia.
Amritha told me that she had being to Australia.
Amritha tell me that she has being to Australia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and needs to be converted into indirect speech.
 
• The verb "**have been**" in present perfect changes to "**had been**" in past perfect in indirect speech.
 
• The correct transformation is: "**Amritha told me that she had been to Australia.**"
 
• **Option 1** correctly follows these rules and accurately represents the indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Amritha told me that she had been to Australia."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: ** "Amritha told me that she has be to Australia." – Incorrect because of the incorrect verb form "has be".
 
• **Option 3: ** "Amritha told me that she had being to Australia." – Incorrect grammar, "had being" is not correct.
 
• **Option 4: ** "Amritha tell me that she has being to Australia." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement and incorrect verb form "has being".

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The insect bit the little baby

options.text: The little baby was bitten by the insect.
The little baby is bitten by the insect.
The little baby has bitten by the insect.
The little baby had bitten by the insect.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change an active voice sentence to passive voice, the object of the active sentence (the little baby) becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb "**bit**" in past simple is changed to "**was bitten**" in passive voice.
 
• The subject of the active sentence (the insect) becomes the agent of the passive sentence, introduced by "**by**".
 
• The correct passive sentence is: "**The little baby was bitten by the insect.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The little baby was bitten by the insect."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: ** "The little baby is bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because it uses the present tense "is bitten" instead of past tense "was bitten".
 
• **Option 3: ** "The little baby has bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because "has bitten" is a present perfect form, which is not suitable here.
 
• **Option 4: ** "The little baby had bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because it incorrectly uses "had bitten" which is past perfect without the auxiliary "been".
